title: "An NA can still count as two characters"
ref: LEN-10
categories: [Empty and NA]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'nzchar(NA)'
reponse: 'TRUE'
attendu: "`NA`, the length of an unknown value is unknown"
versions: "nchar(NA) was 2 up to R 3.2, it has been NA since R 3.3.0 except for type = \"width\""
source: "The R Inferno, R 3.3.0 NEWS"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
nchar(NA)
nchar(NA, type = "width")
nzchar(NA)

first_name <- c("Ana", NA)
nchar(paste(first_name, "Martin"))
```
:::

## Why

Up to R 3.2, `nchar(NA)` was 2: R counted the characters of the printed "NA". R 3.3.0 changed the default, and `nchar(NA)` is now `NA`. But the fix is not complete: with `type = "width"`, the display width, the `NA` still counts as 2, and `nzchar()` still considers that an `NA` is not an empty string.

The most common pitfall today comes from `paste()`, which turns an `NA` into the text `"NA"`. After that, nothing tells it apart from a real two-letter name.

## The remedy

Ask explicitly to keep the `NA`s, and handle them before pasting text.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
nzchar(NA, keepNA = TRUE)
ifelse(is.na(first_name), yes = NA, no = nchar(paste(first_name, "Martin")))
```
:::
